why: CI/workflow tooling only — no runtime, order path, strategy config, risk caps, or live-VM mutation. vm-web-api-recover.yml's `issues: types: [opened]` trigger has no label filter, so every issue opened anywhere in the repo enqueues a run of this workflow (the `if:` gate only screens which of those runs actually restarts the unit). The workflow's concurrency group was the single literal string `vm-web-api-recover`; GitHub Actions keeps at most one pending run per group, so a legitimately `vm-web-api-recover`-labelled restart request could be starved behind unrelated issue-open volume with no error and no comment ever posted back. MEASURED 2026-09-29: issue #14078 (a real restart request, opened while diagnosing why ict-web-api's /api/diag/version reported restart_pending=true) sat `queued` for 5+ minutes with zero progress (run 36552764437) while sibling diag-request/system-action runs for the identical issue-open events completed in ~1-2s each; several other runs in the same shared group dated back to 2026-05-15 and had never executed either — this self-heal path has likely been non-functional via the issue-driven trigger for months. Same fix already applied to vm-diag-snapshot.yml on 2026-07-04 for the identical failure shape (BL-20260611-002): the group is now per-issue (`vm-web-api-recover-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.run_id }}`), isolating each dispatch so unrelated issue traffic can no longer block it. workflow_dispatch runs keep an always-unique group via run_id, unchanged.
